items.prompt:
A student is talking about her pet fish. What visual would help most?
A) A drawing of her fish
B) A drawing of a bicycle
items.answer: A) A drawing of her fish

steps: The presentation is about the fish. A drawing of the fish is directly related and helps the audience picture it.

items.prompt:
When should you add a visual to a description?
A) When it helps the audience understand better
B) Always, for every sentence
items.answer: A) When it helps the audience understand better

steps: Visuals should be added 'when appropriate' — when they clarify ideas or help the audience understand. Not every description requires one.

items.prompt:
A student is describing the shape of a star. What would help most?
A) A drawing of a star
B) A drawing of a football
items.answer: A) A drawing of a star

steps: A drawing of a star directly shows the shape being described. A football is unrelated.

items.prompt:
A student shows a photo of a random car during a presentation about elephants. Is this a good visual?
A) Yes — any picture helps
B) No — the visual should match the topic
items.answer: B) No — the visual should match the topic

steps: A visual must be relevant to the topic. A car photo does not help the audience understand anything about elephants.

items.prompt:
Which visual best helps a student explain where Africa is on a map?
A) A globe or world map with Africa highlighted
B) A drawing of a lion
items.answer: A) A globe or world map with Africa highlighted

steps: To explain where a place is, a map is the clearest visual. A lion might be found in Africa but does not show its location.

items.prompt:
A student is describing a rainbow. A drawing of a rainbow with its colors labeled would:
A) Help the audience see the colors
B) Confuse the audience
items.answer: A) Help the audience see the colors

steps: A labeled drawing of a rainbow directly shows the colors in the correct order — a great visual for this description.

items.prompt:
True or False: A visual display for a presentation should always be related to the topic.
A) True
B) False

steps: A visual is only appropriate if it relates to and clarifies the topic being presented.

items.prompt:
A student is describing how a caterpillar turns into a butterfly. What visual would help most?
A) A diagram showing the stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly
B) A drawing of a spaceship
items.answer: A) A diagram showing the stages: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly

steps: A stage diagram directly illustrates the metamorphosis process — exactly what the student is describing.

items.prompt:
Which of these visuals is most appropriate for a presentation about the four seasons?
A) A picture divided into four sections, one for each season
B) A photo of a sandwich
items.answer: A) A picture divided into four sections, one for each season

steps: A four-section picture showing each season directly supports the topic and helps the audience understand the differences.

items.prompt:
A student describes a tall building. She says: 'It is really, really tall.' Would a drawing help?
A) Yes — a drawing showing the building next to a person would show how tall it is.
B) No — drawings never help.
items.answer: A) Yes — a drawing showing the building next to a person would show how tall it is.

steps: A size comparison drawing (building next to a person) clearly shows how tall the building is in a way that words alone ('really, really tall') may not fully convey.

items.prompt:
A student is showing a drawing of a tree during a presentation about trees. The drawing shows the roots, trunk, branches, and leaves labeled. Is this a good visual?
A) Yes — it clarifies all the parts of the tree
B) No — drawings of trees are not useful
items.answer: A) Yes — it clarifies all the parts of the tree

steps: A labeled diagram showing tree parts directly supports a presentation about trees. It clarifies the information.

items.prompt:
Which visual best helps explain what a volcano looks like?
A) A drawing of a volcano showing lava flowing out of the top
B) A drawing of a swimming pool
items.answer: A) A drawing of a volcano showing lava flowing out of the top

steps: The drawing of the volcano with lava directly illustrates the topic. A swimming pool is unrelated.

items.prompt:
A student uses a drawing that does not match her presentation at all. What is the problem?
A) The visual is irrelevant — it does not help the audience understand the topic.
B) There is no problem — any drawing is fine.
items.answer: A) The visual is irrelevant — it does not help the audience understand the topic.

steps: A visual must be appropriate (relevant) to be useful. An unrelated drawing confuses the audience.

items.prompt:
A student describes how to wash your hands. What visual would help most?
A) Step-by-step pictures showing each step of handwashing
B) A drawing of a birthday cake
items.answer: A) Step-by-step pictures showing each step of handwashing

steps: Step-by-step visuals help the audience follow a process. They directly clarify the instructions.

items.prompt:
When you draw something for a presentation, it should:
A) Be colorful but completely unrelated to the topic
B) Help make your ideas clearer to the audience
items.answer: B) Help make your ideas clearer to the audience

steps: The purpose of a visual is to clarify ideas and help the audience understand. Relevance and clarity matter more than decoration.
